metadata.title: Mirvetuximab soravtansine Therapy
metadata.indication: Adult patients with FRα-positive, platinum-resistant high-grade serous epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer following one to three prior systemic regimens.

contexts.duration_text: Every 21 days until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

source_supplements.name: EMA Elahere product information, sections 4.2 and 4.4

encoding_maturity.label: Source-mapped feasibility build; independent clinical and pharmacy review pending

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: A consultant medical oncologist initiates the treatment plan. Discuss dose modifications with the consultant.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Use the most restrictive applicable action and confirm the modified dose and next visit with oncology pharmacy.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Encoded from NCCP 00921 v1. Independent clinical and oncology pharmacy validation is pending.

indications.description: Adult patients with FRα-positive, platinum-resistant high-grade serous epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer following one to three prior systemic regimens.

treatment.schedule_summary: Every 21 days until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. One IV infusion on day 1 at 6 mg/kg adjusted ideal body weight (AIBW).
treatment.dose_basis: Female IBW (kg) = 0.9 × height (cm) − 92. AIBW (kg) = IBW + 0.4 × (actual weight − IBW). A patient aged 18 or older who is 165 cm and 80 kg has an AIBW of 65.9 kg. Confirm the prescribed dose level with pharmacy.

treatment_phases.label: First infusion

administration.note: Start at 1 mg/min. After 30 minutes without intolerance, increase to 3 mg/min. After another 30 minutes if tolerated, increase to 5 mg/min.
administration.diluent: 250 mL glucose 5%. Pharmacy verifies the final concentration of 1–2 mg/mL for the prescribed dose.

notes: Dilute in glucose 5% (final concentration 1–2 mg/mL) and flush with glucose 5%. Use a 0.2 or 0.22 μm PES in-line filter. Avoid DEHP-containing devices and saline.

treatment_phases.label: Subsequent infusion
treatment_phases.duration_text: Cycle 2 onward until progression or unacceptable toxicity

administration.note: Use the highest previously tolerated rate, up to 5 mg/min. Reassess any previous infusion reaction and altered premedication before starting.
administration.diluent: 250 mL glucose 5%. Pharmacy verifies the final concentration of 1–2 mg/mL for the prescribed dose.

notes: Dilute in glucose 5% (final concentration 1–2 mg/mL) and flush with glucose 5%. Use a 0.2 or 0.22 μm PES in-line filter. Avoid DEHP-containing devices and saline.

eligibility: Adult patients with FRα-positive, platinum-resistant high-grade serous epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer following one to three prior systemic regimens.
ECOG 0–2. At least 75% of viable tumour cells show moderate (2+) or strong (3+) membrane staining by validated IHC. NCCP specifies FOLR1 RxDx on the VENTANA platform for baseline testing.
exclusions: Known hypersensitivity to mirvetuximab soravtansine or an excipient.

baseline: FBC, renal and liver profile; FRα tumour assay; visual acuity and slit-lamp examination; pregnancy test when relevant; neuropathy assessment as indicated.
on_treatment: Repeat blood, renal and liver profiles. Review new symptoms before each cycle.

New ocular symptoms need examination and prescriber review before dosing. In grade ≥2 ocular reactions repeat eye assessment at least every other cycle until resolved or at baseline, and sooner if clinically indicated.
Monitor peripheral neuropathy. Record CTCAE v5 grades, eye findings and the current AIBW dose level before applying a modification.

supportive_care.mapping_basis: NCCP 00921 v1 p5 lists moderate emetic risk. Reconcile the NCCP regimen-specific premedications with the local plan.
premedications: Before each infusion NCCP Table 4 gives paracetamol 1 g orally, chlorphenamine 10 mg IV and dexamethasone 10 mg IV at 60 minutes, followed by ondansetron 16 mg orally at 30 minutes. Reconcile overlapping antiemetics before administration.
eye_care: Lubricating drops throughout treatment. Avoid contact lenses. Ophthalmology directs secondary topical steroid prophylaxis after slit-lamp-confirmed grade ≥2 corneal toxicity. Use on infusion day and the next seven days of subsequent cycles as prescribed. Wait at least 15 minutes after the steroid before lubricant drops. Monitor intraocular pressure and slit-lamp findings.

rules.explanation: Monitor grade 1 pneumonitis.

action.message: Grade 3–4 pneumonitis requires permanent discontinuation.

action.message: Withhold for treatment-emergent grade 2 neuropathy until grade ≤1, then reduce one level.

rules.explanation: Withhold for treatment-emergent grade 2 neuropathy until grade ≤1, then reduce one level.

action.message: Treatment-emergent grade 3–4 peripheral neuropathy requires permanent discontinuation.

action.message: Confirm whether this is pretreatment or treatment-emergent neuropathy. Baseline grade ≥2 requires review; on treatment follow Table 3 before another dose.

action.message: Maintain the current infusion rate and monitor a grade 1 reaction.

rules.explanation: Maintain the current infusion rate and monitor a grade 1 reaction.

action.message: Interrupt the infusion and give supportive treatment. After symptoms recover, restart at 50% of the previous rate, then increase if tolerated. For subsequent cycles, review additional dexamethasone 8 mg orally twice the day before treatment, or local equivalent.

action.message: Immediately stop the infusion, give emergency supportive treatment and permanently discontinue for grade 3–4 reaction.

action.message: Withhold for grade 3–4 haematological toxicity; once grade ≤1 resume one level lower.

action.message: Withhold for other grade 3 toxicity until grade ≤1, then reduce one level.

action.message: Permanently discontinue for other grade 4 adverse reactions.

action.message: Permanently discontinue when 4 mg/kg AIBW is not tolerated.
